summary: Baileys fork pulls libsignal from a mutable GitHub branch at install time
details: package.json declares a runtime dependency `libsignal` whose source is `github:dzytzy/alya-baileys#latest` — a mutable branch rather than a pinned version or commit SHA. On `npm install`, npm clones whatever currently lives on that branch and installs it as `libsignal`, running any lifecycle scripts the fetched tree declares. The branch owner can swap the installed code at any time without republishing this package to npm, so install-time code execution on the installer's machine is controlled entirely by whoever controls that branch. Separately, `makeNewsletterSocket` wires a hardcoded `ChannelManager` that, on connection open, silently auto-subscribes the installer's authenticated WhatsApp account to the author-owned newsletter JID `120363411407993897@newsletter` (default-on unless `autoFollowChannels: false` is set), and `fetchLatestBaileysVersion` reads version metadata from `raw.githubusercontent.com/ramadanny/vialeys/refs/heads/master/...` — a mutable branch under a GitHub user unrelated to the declared publisher `dzytzy`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
